extracted.intended_audience: users of GAP (computational algebra system), mathematicians and programmers working with transformations, semigroups, and partial permutations
extracted.subtask_description: Reference material describing GAP functions, attributes, and conventions for transformations, transformation semigroups, and partial permutations; includes definitions, return values, optional arguments, display preferences, and examples of usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsInjectiveListTrans
rubrics_metrics.description: Checks injectivity of a transformation on a given list: the argument obj should be a transformation or the list of images of a transformation and list should be a list of positive integers. If obj is a transformation, define f := obj; if obj is the image list of a transformation define f := Transformation(obj). Returns true if f is injective on list and false otherwise. If list is not duplicate free then false is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate behavior on transformations and image-lists; e.g. IsInjectiveListTrans([1,5], f) true, but if list contains duplicates like [5,1,5,1,1] it returns false.

rubrics_metrics.name: ComponentTransformationInt
rubrics_metrics.description: ComponentTransformationInt(f, n) returns the elements i such that n^f^j = i for some positive integer j — the component of f containing n obtained by applying powers of f to n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a list of positive integers; example: ComponentTransformationInt(f,1) -> [1,6,5,7,8,3]. If n is not moved, returns [n].

rubrics_metrics.name: PreImagesOfTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: PreImagesOfTransformation(f, n) returns the preimages (set of positive integers i such that i^f = n) of the positive integer n under the transformation f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a set; examples show PreImagesOfTransformation(f,1) -> [8,9], PreImagesOfTransformation(f,100) -> [100] (fixed point outside defined images).

rubrics_metrics.name: DegreeOfTransformation / DegreeOfTransformationCollection
rubrics_metrics.description: DegreeOfTransformation(f) returns the degree of a transformation f: the least n such that [n+1, n+2, ...] is fixed pointwise by f (equivalently largest value such that some i^f <> i or i^f = n for some i <> n). DegreeOfTransformationCollection(coll) returns the maximum degree of any transformation in coll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a non-negative integer. Examples: DegreeOfTransformation(IdentityTransformation) -> 0; DegreeOfTransformationCollection([t1,t2,t3]) returns the maximum degree among t1,t2,t3.

rubrics_metrics.name: ImageListOfTransformation / ListTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: ImageListOfTransformation(f[, n]) (alias ListTransformation) returns the list of images of [1..n] under f, i.e. [1^f .. n^f]. If n omitted, the degree of f is used by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogue of ListPerm for permutations. Examples: ImageListOfTransformation(f) -> [2,3,4,2,4]; ImageListOfTransformation(f,10) appends images for points beyond degree (fixed by default).

rubrics_metrics.name: ImageSetOfTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: ImageSetOfTransformation(f[, n]) returns the sorted list of images of [1..n] under f with duplicates removed. If n omitted, the degree of f is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a set-like list; examples: ImageSetOfTransformation(f) -> [1,2,3,4,5,6,7]; ImageSetOfTransformation(f,10) may include additional fixed points.

rubrics_metrics.name: RankOfTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: RankOfTransformation(f[, n]) or RankOfTransformation(f, list) returns the rank of transformation f. With a positive integer n, returns the size of the set of images of f in [1..n] (degree used if n omitted). With a list of positive integers, returns the size of the set of images of f on that list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: RankOfTransformation(f) -> 7; RankOfTransformation(f,100) -> 97; RankOfTransformation(f,[2,5,8]) -> 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: MovedPoints
rubrics_metrics.description: MovedPoints(f) returns the set of positive integers i such that i^f <> i. MovedPoints(coll) returns the set of points moved by some element of the collection coll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns an empty list for identity transformation. Example: MovedPoints(f) -> [1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9,10].

rubrics_metrics.name: NrMovedPoints
rubrics_metrics.description: NrMovedPoints(f) returns the number of positive integers i such that i^f <> i. NrMovedPoints(coll) returns the number of points moved by at least one element of the collection coll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a non-negative integer. Example: NrMovedPoints(f) -> 9; NrMovedPoints(IdentityTransformation) -> 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: SmallestMovedPoint
rubrics_metrics.description: SmallestMovedPoint(f) returns the smallest positive integer i such that i^f <> i, or infinity if f is identity. For a collection coll, returns the smallest point moved by at least one element, or infinity if none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns positive integer or infinity. Examples: SmallestMovedPoint(FullTransformationSemigroup(5)) -> 1; SmallestMovedPoint(Semigroup(IdentityTransformation)) -> infinity.

rubrics_metrics.name: LargestMovedPoint
rubrics_metrics.description: LargestMovedPoint(f) returns the largest positive integer i such that i^f <> i, or 0 if f is identity. For a collection coll, returns the largest point moved by at least one element, or 0 if none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns non-negative integer. Examples: LargestMovedPoint(FullTransformationSemigroup(5)) -> 5; LargestMovedPoint(IdentitySemigroup) -> 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: SmallestImageOfMovedPoint
rubrics_metrics.description: SmallestImageOfMovedPoint(f) returns the smallest positive integer i^f such that i^f <> i, or infinity if f is identity. For a collection coll, returns the smallest image of a point moved by at least one element, or infinity if none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns positive integer or infinity. Example: SmallestImageOfMovedPoint(FullTransformationSemigroup(5)) -> 1; SmallestImageOfMovedPoint(Identity) -> infinity.

rubrics_metrics.name: LargestImageOfMovedPoint
rubrics_metrics.description: LargestImageOfMovedPoint(f) returns the largest positive integer i^f such that i^f <> i, or 0 if f is identity. For a collection coll, returns the largest image of a point moved by at least one element, or 0 if none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns non-negative integer. Example: LargestImageOfMovedPoint(f) -> 6 for sample f.

rubrics_metrics.name: FlatKernelOfTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: FlatKernelOfTransformation(f[, n]) returns a list L such that L[i] = j for all i in K_j where K1,...,Kr are the kernel classes of f on [1..n]. For a given transformation and n, there is a unique such list. If n omitted, degree of f used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a list encoding kernel class indices; example: FlatKernelOfTransformation(f) -> [1,2,3,1,4,5,6,7,8,1].

rubrics_metrics.name: KernelOfTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: KernelOfTransformation(f[, n, bool]) returns the kernel of f on [1..n] as a set of sets of positive integers. If bool is false, only non-singleton classes are returned. Defaults: n = degree of f, bool = true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: KernelOfTransformation(f) -> [ [1,4], [2,5], [3], ... ]. KernelOfTransformation(f,5,false) -> only non-singleton classes within [1..5].

rubrics_metrics.name: InverseOfTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: InverseOfTransformation(f) returns a semigroup inverse g of f in the full transformation semigroup: any g such that f*g*f = f and g*f*g = g. Every transformation has at least one inverse; returned object is a transformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not the same as bijective inverse; example: InverseOfTransformation(f) -> some transformation g satisfying semigroup inverse identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse (for a transformation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inverse(f) or f^-1 returns the inverse of f if f is a bijection; if f is not a bijection then fail is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the group-theoretic inverse (exists only for bijections). Example: Transformation([2,3,1])^-1 -> Transformation([3,1,2]); Transformation([...])^-1 may return fail if not bijection.

rubrics_metrics.name: IndexPeriodOfTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: IndexPeriodOfTransformation(f) returns the least positive integers m and r (index and period) such that f^(m+r) = f^m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a pair [m,r]. Examples: IndexPeriodOfTransformation(f) -> [2,3]; IdentityTransformation -> [1,1].

rubrics_metrics.name: SmallestIdempotentPower
rubrics_metrics.description: SmallestIdempotentPower(f) returns the least positive integer n such that f^n is idempotent. It equals the least multiple of the period of f that is >= the index of f (see IndexPeriodOfTransformation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns positive integer. Examples: SmallestIdempotentPower(f) -> 3 or 2 depending on f.

rubrics_metrics.name: ComponentsOfTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: ComponentsOfTransformation(f) returns a list of the components of the functional digraph of f; each component is a subset of [1..DegreeOfTransformation(f)] and the union of components is [1..DegreeOfTransformation(f)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a list of lists of positive integers. Examples: ComponentsOfTransformation(f) -> [ [1,6,4,9], [2,12,3,11,5,7,10], [8] ].

rubrics_metrics.name: NrComponentsOfTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: NrComponentsOfTransformation(f) returns the number of components of f on the range [1..DegreeOfTransformation(f)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns positive integer; example NrComponentsOfTransformation(f) -> 3 or 4 depending on f.

rubrics_metrics.name: ComponentRepsOfTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: ComponentRepsOfTransformation(f) returns representatives of the components of f: for every i in [1..DegreeOfTransformation(f)] there exists a representative j and k>0 such that i^(f^k)=j. Representatives are partitioned by component and the function returns the least number of representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns list of lists of representatives; examples provided showing one representative per cycle/component.

rubrics_metrics.name: CyclesOfTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: CyclesOfTransformation(f[, list]) returns a list of the cycles of the components of f that contain any element of list. If list omitted, [1..DegreeOfTransformation(f)] is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns list of lists (cycles). Example: CyclesOfTransformation(f) -> [ [6], [12], [8] ]. Passing an extended range may return additional fixed-point cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: CycleTransformationInt
rubrics_metrics.description: CycleTransformationInt(f, n) returns the cycle of the component of f containing n (the cyclic part reached by following f-powers starting from n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns list of positive integers; example CycleTransformationInt(f,1) -> [8,3], CycleTransformationInt(f,12) -> [12].

rubrics_metrics.name: LeftOne / RightOne (for a transformation)
rubrics_metrics.description: LeftOne(f) returns an idempotent e such that kernel(e) (w.r.t degree of f) equals kernel(f) and e * f = f. RightOne(f) returns an idempotent e such that image_set(e) equals image_set(f) and f * e = f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned e is idempotent; examples show RightOne(f) and LeftOne(f) produce idempotents satisfying the identities e*f = f or f*e = f and IsIdempotent(e) -> true.

rubrics_metrics.name: TrimTransformation
rubrics_metrics.description: TrimTransformation(f[, n]) changes the internal representation of f to remove trailing fixed points to reduce memory usage; if n provided, internal representation reduced to images of first n points. The operation modifies f in-place and returns nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: if optional n provided it must hold that i^f <= n for all i in [1..n] otherwise the resulting object will not define a transformation. Example demonstrates reducing memory usage and DegreeOfTransformation changing after trimming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displaying transformations (preferences)
rubrics_metrics.description: User preferences control how GAP displays transformations: TransformationDisplayLimit (default 100) determines whether a transformation is displayed as '<transformation on n pts with rank r>' (if degree > limit) or expanded. NotationForTransformations has two values: one displays as Transformation(ImageListOfTransformation(f,n)) except identity which is IdentityTransformation; the other displays as '<transformation: ImageList>' where n is largest moved point (identity shown as '<identity transformation>').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show SetUserPreference("TransformationDisplayLimit",12) and SetUserPreference("NotationForTransformations","fr").

rubrics_metrics.name: Semigroups package capabilities (transformations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Semigroups GAP package provides many additional functions and more efficient methods for creating and computing properties of semigroups of transformations (e.g., Green's classes, size, elements, group of units, minimal ideal, small generating sets, membership testing, inverses of regular elements, factorization over generators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that transformation semigroups are also transformation collections so special methods for MovedPoints, NrMovedPoints, LargestMovedPoint, SmallestMovedPoint, LargestImageOfMovedPoint, SmallestImageOfMovedPoint apply to semigroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsTransformationSemigroup / IsTransformationMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: IsTransformationSemigroup(obj) returns true if obj is a semigroup consisting of transformations: it must satisfy IsSemigroup and IsTransformationCollection. IsTransformationMonoid(obj) (synonym) returns true if obj is a monoid consisting of transformations: it must satisfy IsMonoid and IsTransformationCollection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: possible for semigroup to have multiplicative neutral element but not satisfy IsTransformationMonoid in some contexts; examples illustrate subtlety with One(S) and MultiplicativeNeutralElement(S).

rubrics_metrics.name: DegreeOfTransformationSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: DegreeOfTransformationSemigroup(S) returns the degree of a transformation semigroup S: the maximum of the degrees of elements of S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns non-negative integer. Example: for semigroup S with certain generators, DegreeOfTransformationSemigroup(S) -> 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: FullTransformationSemigroup / FullTransformationMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: FullTransformationSemigroup(n) (alias FullTransformationMonoid) returns the monoid consisting of all transformations with degree at most n (the full transformation semigroup). It is regular, has n^n elements, and is generated by any set containing generators for symmetric group on n points and any transformation of rank n-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: FullTransformationSemigroup(1234) -> <full transformation monoid of degree 1234>.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsFullTransformationSemigroup / IsFullTransformationMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: IsFullTransformationSemigroup(S) returns true iff the transformation semigroup S of degree n contains every transformation of degree at most n. IsFullTransformationMonoid is a synonym.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show constructing S and testing IsFullTransformationSemigroup(S) true; notes common literature interchange of 'monoid' and 'semigroup' for full transformation monoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsomorphismTransformationSemigroup / IsomorphismTransformationMonoid
rubrics_metrics.description: IsomorphismTransformationSemigroup(S) returns an isomorphism from a finite semigroup S to a transformation semigroup (often right regular representation acting on S^1, degree usually |S|+1). IsomorphismTransformationMonoid differs only in returning an isomorphism to a transformation monoid when S is a monoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: if S is a permutation group or a partial perm semigroup, natural faithful action on largest moved point may be used; finitely presented semigroups use Todd-Coxeter approach. Examples show returned MappingByFunction objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: AntiIsomorphismTransformationSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: AntiIsomorphismTransformationSemigroup(S) returns an anti-isomorphism from S to a transformation semigroup; currently degree of resulting semigroup equals |S|+1, so limited in use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows mapping to much larger-degree semigroup may be produced; returns MappingByFunction object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental attributes of a partial permutation
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental attributes of a partial permutation f in GAP: Domain (dom(f)) is the set of positive integers where f is defined; Degree is the largest element in domain (DegreeOfPartialPerm); Image list is [i1^f, i2^f, .., in^f] where domain is [i1,..,in] (ImageListOfPartialPerm); Image set is the sorted image list with duplicates removed (ImageSetOfPartialPerm); Codegree is largest i^f among images (CodegreeOfPartialPerm); Rank is size of domain (or equivalently size of image set/image list) (RankOfPartialPerm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These attributes correspond to the representation of partial permutations as functional digraphs; examples and function references are given in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional digraph and components of a partial permutation
rubrics_metrics.description: A partial permutation can be seen as a functional digraph with vertices [1..DegreeOfPartialPerm(f)] and edges i -> i^f for every i in domain. Components are defined by connectivity allowing traversal along edges or reverse edges: i and j are in same component iff there is a path using i^f or inverse edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Components correspond to connected components of this digraph; used in functions computing components, cycles, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse of a partial permutation (unique semigroup inverse)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a partial permutation f the inverse f^-1 maps i^f to i for all i in domain. Domain(f^-1) = image(f), image(f^-1) = domain(f). f^-1 is the unique partial permutation satisfying f*f^-1*f = f and f^-1*f*f^-1 = f^-1; thus the unique semigroup inverse in the symmetric inverse monoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inverse exists and is unique because partial permutations form an inverse monoid; can obtain using f^-1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product domain/image formulas for partial permutations
rubrics_metrics.description: If f and g are partial permutations, then dom(fg) = (im(f) ∩ dom(g)) f^{-1} and im(fg) = (im(f) ∩ dom(g)) g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives exact formula for domain and image of the product fg; useful when reasoning about composition of partial permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idempotents, left/right one, one, and multiplicative zero for partial permutations
rubrics_metrics.description: A partial permutation is idempotent iff it is the identity function on its domain. For f, f*f^-1 and f^-1*f are the identity on domain(f) and image(f) respectively; these are the left one and right one of f. The one of a partial permutation is the identity on the union of its domain and image; the zero is the empty partial permutation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LeftOne and RightOne functions return these idempotents; One and MultiplicativeZero functions referenced for monoid/semigroup identity/zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal representation and storage of partial permutations in GAP
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP stores a partial permutation f as a list consisting of codegree and images i^f for points <= degree; 0 stored where i^f is undefined. Domain and image set are cached and stored when computed. If codegree < 65536 values stored as 16-bit integers (IsPPerm2Rep), otherwise 32-bit (IsPPerm4Rep). Domain and image set are stored as immutable plain lists of GAP integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implications: representation affects memory usage and performance; Trim-like routines exist elsewhere to adjust representation for transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPartialPerm (category test)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPartialPerm(obj) returns true if obj is a partial permutation in GAP. Basic operations for partial permutations include DomainOfPartialPerm, ImageListOfPartialPerm, ImageSetOfPartialPerm, DegreeOfPartialPerm, RankOfPartialPerm; multiplication via *, exponentiation for action; inverse via f^-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category membership indicates available methods and attributes for the object.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPartialPermCollection (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPartialPermCollection(obj) returns true if obj is a collection of partial permutations (e.g., a semigroup of partial permutations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections of partial permutations support collection-level methods and attributes analogous to transformation collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: PartialPermFamily
rubrics_metrics.description: PartialPermFamily is the GAP family object representing the family of all partial permutations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used internally/for category hierarchy; indicates where partial permutations sit in GAP's type system.

rubrics_metrics.name: PartialPerm (constructors)
rubrics_metrics.description: PartialPerm(dom, img) or PartialPerm(list) constructs a partial permutation. Two forms: (1) domain/image form where dom is a set of positive integers and img is a duplicate-free list; the partial perm maps dom[i] -> img[i]. (2) dense image list form: a list where entry list[i] = image of i or 0 if undefined; maps i -> list[i] when list[i] <> 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing representation: if largest domain point >> rank, use domain/image version to avoid huge lists; for dense domains use dense image list. Examples: PartialPerm([1,5],[20,2]) and PartialPerm([20,0,0,0,2]). Regardless of construction method, internal representation is the same.
